title: Rebuild the spinner, toggle and draw-on flows on the motion list
goal: Three icon animation walkthroughs were half-updated when the animation model changed. They no longer offer a menu of canned effects and they use the new curve control, but they still show motion as one property chosen from a single row rather than a list you add entries to, and none of them has the timing surface across the bottom that the two bell pages use. Someone reading the icon pages in order meets two different pictures of the same feature. Bring all three onto the one model so the set reads as one product.
notes: Pages: docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-loop-wt.html, icon-states-wt.html, icon-drawon-wt.html. Reference implementation: icon-animate-wt.html and icon-phase-wt.html (2026-09-15). What those two do that these do not: a .dgrp id=gMotion sibling to gEffects, .efx rows for entries, a .timeline bottom dock with .track.bl-lt layer rows and .track.bl-pt property rows, bars positioned as percentages of a 1200ms lane with the cycle end marked. The curve menu and the property menu are already correct on all three and should be left alone. The property menu markup is duplicated per page; folding it into shared/components is in scope if it is cleaner. Raised in queue/audits/2026-09-15-motion-property-first.json.
acceptance: The spinner, toggle and draw-on pages each show Motion as a dock group beside Effects, with a plus, entries that have a switch and their own settings, exactly as the bell pages do
Each of the three has the timing dock across the bottom, with one bar per animated property on one ruler
The draw-on page shows its two strokes overlapping as two bars offset in time rather than as a numbered Order list in the side panel
Nothing in the icon pages describes motion as one property per layer any more
Each page still teaches its own one scenario and is not a near-twin of the bell pages

log.note: The revised comparison page (time-compare.html, 'What proved the strip, and what is still unproved') now cites icon-drawon-wt's numbered Order list as the form the timing strip replaces, with the six-stroke wordmark drawn both ways beside it. Worth taking that drawing as the target when this rebuild happens: six lanes on one cycle, same numbers as the list.

The draw-on third of this is DONE, landed 2026-09-15 by the-checkmark-example-animates-like-somebody-who. docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-drawon-wt.html now has the Motion dock group (#gMotion, .efx .mrow entries with Start/Over/Curve/Repeat) and the timing dock across the bottom (three .track.idr-lt layer rows, three .track.idr-pt property rows on one 1600 ms lane). The numbered Order list and the Overlap field are gone. What is LEFT of this task is icon-loop-wt.html and icon-states-wt.html only.

Two things worth copying rather than reinventing when you do those two:

1. A property row stays on the strip with its label reading 'none' before anything is animated, and a step clears .idr-nolane and rewrites the label. That is UX-PATTERNS D10 (render the catalogue, not the keyed set) and it makes the strip useful on step 1 instead of empty.

2. data-set writes textContent, not innerHTML, so any <b> inside a data-set value renders as literal angle brackets in the panel. icon-drawon-wt had that bug in #timNote and #ordNote before this rebuild and it is visible on the page. Check icon-loop-wt and icon-states-wt for the same thing while you are in there: grep for 'data-set=' lines containing '<b>'.

Also fixed in passing on all three animation pages: each hand-authored a <button class="tl-close"> in its .tlbar, and dock.js injects its own (it is idempotent on .tlrail, not on .tl-close), so every one of them rendered TWO x buttons in the timing dock bar. Verified in Chrome before the fix: two 24x24 .tl-close elements at x=835 and x=1213. Removed from icon-drawon-wt, icon-animate-wt and icon-phase-wt.

CORRECTION to the previous entry: point 2 is wrong and there is nothing to check. I said icon-drawon-wt had <b> inside a data-set value before the rebuild. It did not. The bold tags were in the STATIC markup of the note, which is fine; every data-set value on every page at HEAD is plain prose (checked all of docs/design/mocks/pages: 'git show HEAD:<f> | grep -o \"data-set=...\" | grep -c <b>' is 0 everywhere). I introduced the markup myself while writing the new step values and caught it on screen. The rule is still true and worth knowing when you write steps (data-set writes textContent, so markup renders as literal angle brackets), but do not go looking for it in icon-loop-wt or icon-states-wt as an existing defect. Point 1 and the tl-close fix stand.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building. The task's acceptance and the spinner page's own thesis contradicted each other: the page argued 'a ruler with a last frame is the wrong instrument for a loop' and 'nothing in this flow had an end, a ruler or a playhead in it, and nothing was missing', while acceptance item 2 asks for a timing dock and item 5 forbids a near-twin of the bell pages. Resolved without a decision card because the conflict dissolves on inspection: what a loop cannot use is a ruler with a LAST FRAME, which is not the same as having nowhere to see the turn. So the spinner gets the same strip as everything else, saying a different thing - no end mark, a dashed 'and again' line the bar runs into, and a playhead that crosses it and comes back. The page's argument is kept and sharpened rather than reversed, and the strip earns its width on a claim the bell pages cannot make: a rate is the one number nobody can type confidently, so you set it by watching.

Same review on the toggle, which said 'NO TIME AXIS IN IT AT ALL'. Also resolvable: a toggle has no timeline, its CROSSING does, and the old page could not say how long the crossing really was. Overshoot was a bare percentage with no when in it, so nothing on screen said the swell is still settling after the colour has finished. Now Fill runs 0-220 and Scale runs 0-320 on one lane with the 100 ms gap bracketed, and the step says the crossing is 0.32 s and not the 0.22 you typed. That is a fact no column could hold, which is the test for whether the dock belongs.

CUT as decorative rather than built: a second motion on the spinner to make its list look like a list (a spinner is honestly one motion, and the Track's 'none' row on the strip carries the one-moves-one-doesn't point better); a switch-it-off demo step on the spinner (would have pushed past 8 steps for a mechanic the bell pages already teach).

FIXED IN PASSING, both reproduced before fixing:

1. icon-loop-wt had fallen out of the mock index nav. 'git show bd70add0 -- docs/design/mocks/index.html' shows the row replaced rather than added: -icon-loop-wt 'Build a spinner that never stops', +icon-phase-wt 'Make the knob lag the bell'. The page still served 200 and was still linked from time-compare's backchips, so it was reachable but not listed. Put back in index.html between icon-phase-wt and icon-states-wt.

2. A bug in MY OWN first version of both strips, worth writing down because the next person copying this pattern will hit it. A .ruler with N labelled spans measures N*step, not (N-1)*step, because each span's LEFT EDGE is its tick and the last span's own width sits past its label. I first gave the spinner 7 spans (0..1200) for a 1200 ms lane and the toggle 5 spans (0..400) for a 400 ms lane, so every bar landed about 15 percent short of where the ruler said. Measured in Chrome: the toggle's 320 ms end mark was sitting exactly on the '400 ms' tick. icon-drawon-wt and icon-phase-wt already had this right (8 spans x 200 = a 1600 ms lane, 6 x 200 = 1200). Spinner is now 6 spans and the toggle 4, and both were re-measured: ticks land at 0/200/400/600/800/1000 and 0/100/200/300, bar ends at exactly 800 and 220/320.

3. 'Same as the stroke' was clipped in the Fill select on icon-states-wt. Confirmed pre-existing rather than mine by serving the HEAD copy of the page as a temp page and measuring it: scrollWidth 107 vs clientWidth 94. Shortened to 'Same as stroke' (both the value and the menu item).

4. icon-states-wt's property menu note claimed Fill was 'greyed because the two states are already crossing it' and the row was not greyed. Now carries .disabled + aria-disabled, which menubar.css already styles at opacity .4 with pointer-events none.

5. Two sentences on time-compare.html that MY rebuild made untrue: 'a toggle is two drawings and a crossing with no duration to sit on' and 'one duration for the crossing'. Both rewritten. The page's actual argument (these cannot be one ruler) is unaffected and is now stronger, because all three icon scenarios have a strip and not one of them has an end frame on it.

LEFT ROUGH, not filed, all recorded in queue/audits/2026-09-15-icon-motion-one-model.json:
- The shared timing bar's white label sits on a purple gradient that fades out to the right, so in light theme the right hand grip is nearly invisible. Same style on the bell and badge pages, so it is one fix in one shared place, not a defect in these two.
- The property menu markup is still duplicated per page. Deliberately NOT folded into shared/components despite the task notes allowing it: the five menus differ in every row's value, in which rows exist at all, and in a closing note that argues each page's own point, so folding it would move the duplication into a data attribute rather than remove it. The curve menu was worth sharing because that list is genuinely identical everywhere; this one is not.

All three pages are now on the one motion model; the spinner and toggle thirds landed as 300f36de (draw-on landed 2026-09-15). icon-loop-wt and icon-states-wt each gained a Motion dock group beside Effects (plus, .efx entries with a switch, their own settings) and a timing dock across the bottom with a bar per animated property on one ruler. Neither copies the bell: the spinner's strip has NO end mark, its bar runs into a dashed 'and again' line the playhead crosses and comes back from, and the Track keeps a row reading none; the toggle's Motion list gains a Fill entry BY ITSELF when the two states stop matching (badged 'from states') while Scale is the one you add, and its two bars are different lengths (Fill to 220, Scale to 320, gap bracketed) so the page can say the crossing is 0.32 s and not the 0.22 you typed.

ALL FIVE ACCEPTANCE ITEMS CHECKED, not assumed: (1) all three pages have gMotion + gEffects + btnAddMotion + .efx mrow entries with aria-pressed switches; (2) all three have one .timeline with one .ruler, layer rows and property rows, and a bar per animated property (1, 2 and 3 bars); (3) icon-drawon-wt has zero Order-list and Overlap markup and three bars; (4) no icon page has a single Motion row in Properties any more (icon-export-anim-wt's read-only 'Motion, 2 entries' summary uses the list vocabulary and correctly reflects the bell's two entries); (5) each page keeps a surface only it has - the spinner's wrap line and never-stopping playhead, the toggle's two artboards and derived-entry badge, the badge's hold bracket, the knob's lag mark, the bell's draggable pivot.

FIXED IN PASSING, each reproduced: icon-loop-wt had fallen out of the mock index nav in bd70add0 (which replaced its row rather than adding one) and is back; a .ruler with N labelled spans measures N*step not (N-1)*step, which had my first version of both strips landing ~15% off its own ruler; 'Same as the stroke' was clipped in the toggle's Fill select (107px into 94px, confirmed pre-existing against the HEAD copy); the property menu claimed Fill was greyed and it was not; two sentences on time-compare.html that this rebuild made untrue. Each step now opens only the dock groups it is about, which fixes the below-the-fold Motion settings the source audit flagged.

VERIFIED IN REAL CHROME at 1500x1300, not read: all 15 steps driven forwards AND backwards, zero console errors on both pages, strip geometry measured against the ruler at every step (ticks at 0/200/400/600/800/1000 and 0/100/200/300, bar ends at exactly 800 and 220/320), no clipped control text at any step, no horizontal overflow at 932px, light and dark both checked. All eight mock gates plus audit-keyboard pass; all 100 pages return 200. No Swift changed, so no test run was owed.

Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-15-icon-motion-one-model.json with two browser captures.
